title: Post-training & Preference Learning
description: Study supervised instruction fine-tuning, reward models and preference labels, rlhf and policy constraints, and direct preference optimization. Each lesson includes a worked example and an applied practice task.

lessons.title: Supervised instruction fine-tuning
lessons.description: Design a small instruction dataset and mark the tokens included in its loss.
lessons.conceptOverview: SFT trains on curated instruction-response examples. The loss mask defines which tokens contribute: some recipes supervise assistant responses while treating instructions as context. Data quality, coverage, and formatting determine behavior more directly than the label 'instruction data'.
lessons.whyItMatters: Define supervision and formatting explicitly for the intended assistant behavior.

lessons.title: Reward models and preference labels
lessons.description: Create paired responses where verbosity and correctness disagree and evaluate the preference rubric.
lessons.conceptOverview: Preference data compares alternatives under a specified rubric. A reward model approximates these judgments and can exploit superficial correlations. Evaluate agreement across annotators, distribution shifts, and adversarial responses before treating its score as a reliable objective.
lessons.whyItMatters: Reward scores are learned proxies that require independent validation.

lessons.title: RLHF and policy constraints
lessons.description: Explain the roles of policy, reference, reward model, and held-out human evaluation.
lessons.conceptOverview: RLHF commonly combines a reference policy, a learned reward, and an optimization procedure that changes the policy. Constraints or penalties can limit drift from a reference. Optimizing a proxy too aggressively can harm behavior that the reward does not capture.
lessons.whyItMatters: Monitor independent behavior measures during reward optimization.

lessons.title: Direct preference optimization
lessons.description: Audit preference pairs for inconsistent rubrics before comparing a DPO run with its base model.
lessons.conceptOverview: DPO uses preferred and dispreferred responses to optimize a relative preference objective without requiring the same explicit online reward-optimization loop as common RLHF recipes. It still depends on preference quality, a reference policy formulation, and hyperparameter choices.
lessons.whyItMatters: A simpler optimization pipeline does not remove dependence on preference-data quality.
